disease.inheritance: Autosomal co-dominant — SERPINA1 Z allele (Glu342Lys, the PI*Z variant) homozygosity is the most common severe form
disease.mechanism: Dual mechanism. (1) Gain-of-function in the liver: the Z-variant alpha-1-antitrypsin misfolds and polymerizes, accumulating in hepatocyte endoplasmic reticulum, causing liver injury, fibrosis, and cirrhosis. (2) Loss-of-function in the lung: reduced circulating A1AT (a serine protease inhibitor) leaves the lung unprotected from neutrophil elastase, causing early-onset emphysema. The liver toxicity is the toxic-gain-of-function component.
disease.autotac_rationale: COMPLEX — NOT a blanket 'eligible'. The liver disease is a toxic gain-of-function (Z-AAT polymerization), so a selective degrader of polymerized Z-AAT is mechanistically plausible for the HEPATIC component. However the lung disease is loss-of-function (deficient antiprotease), where degradation would worsen it. AUTOTAC is NOT appropriate for the disease as a whole — only a targeted hepatic strategy would qualify. The approved therapy is augmentation (restore the missing antiprotease), which addresses the LoF component.
disease.prevalence: ~1 in 2,500-5,000 (PI*ZZ, European descent) — commonly cited; UNVERIFIED exact figure this session
disease.age_of_onset: Lung: early adulthood (emphysema, worse with smoking); Liver: infancy (cholestatic jaundice) to adulthood (cirrhosis)

approved_treatments.drug: Alpha-1 Proteinase Inhibitor (human, e.g. Prolastin-C / Zemaira / Aralast)
approved_treatments.mechanism_correct: Intravenous infusion of purified human alpha-1-antitrypsin to restore circulating antiprotease levels, protecting the lung from elastase-mediated damage. Addresses the loss-of-function component only; does not clear hepatic Z-AAT polymers.
approved_treatments.note: NOTE: A1AT augmentation is a pooled human plasma-derived protein (~52 kDa), NOT a small molecule — MW/PubChem CID left 0 to avoid fabrication.

investigational: Small-molecule polymerisation blockers (e.g. targeting the Z-AAT polymer interface — JCI Insight 2025)
Selective degraders of polymerized Z-AAT (autophagy enhancers / PROTAC) — preclinical, for the hepatic component
siRNA silencing of SERPINA1 (e.g. fazirsiran/ARO-AAT — clinical)

disease.human_summary: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency is an autosomal co-dominant disorder caused by the SERPINA1 Z allele, whose protein product polymerizes and accumulates in the liver (causing cirrhosis) while deficient circulating antiprotease leaves the lungs vulnerable to emphysema. It is a dual gain-of-function (liver) and loss-of-function (lung) disease; augmentation therapy treats the lung component.
